description: Maps this grammar's ANTLR rule names onto flix-spec's canonical TreeKind vocabulary. Written by starting empty and working down the report's frequency-ranked `unmapped` list, which is the workflow flix-spec's docs/CONFORMANCE.md prescribes: map what is genuinely the same node, declare our own wrappers transparent, and leave the rest unmapped rather than guessing -- a wrong mapping reports as agreement and is worse than a gap.

notes.AddExpr: Stands for every binary label (UserOpExpr, AngledPlusExpr, MultExpr, AddExpr, ConsExpr, CompareExpr, EqualityExpr, AndExpr, OrExpr). The projection now emits labelled-alternative names instead of the shared rule name, so expr, type and pattern are never emitted and each label is keyed on its own. They start in `ignored`, which is exactly how `expr` behaved. Mapping them onto Expr.Binary waits for the synthetic Operator node: Expr.Binary has canonical arity 3 (lhs, Operator, rhs) and this projection emits no token children, so without it every binary node would diverge on arity. That also answers the old note on expr, which recorded that mapping the branching case to Expr.Binary raised depth 88% -> 94% and dropped agreement 76 -> 40: it was not a bad guess, it was a missing node.
notes.CommentList: The one elide this map keeps, and the one exception to elide-nothing-Flix-does-not. The reference emits CommentList wherever comments appear; this grammar routes comments to the COMMENTS and DOC_COMMENTS channels, so they never reach the parse tree and no rule of ours can stand for the node. That is a kind this consumer genuinely cannot produce, which docs/PROJECTION.md admits, rather than a structure we choose not to model. It goes when Projection.kt splices the off-channel tokens back into position -- the same work that would let token-accounting and token-positions run.
notes.declaration: A wrapper around every declaration together with its doc, annotations and modifiers, where the reference makes those direct children of Decl.Def. Transparent at arity <= 1 and spliced by `declPrefix` otherwise.
notes.definitionName: A wrapper around the name rule, where the reference's Ident holds its token directly. Mapping both onto Ident gave Ident-inside-Ident and an arity divergence on every declaration -- 126 of them, the single largest class in the first measurement.
notes.expr: Emitted only for a bare ExprContext, which ANTLR leaves behind when error recovery abandons a left-recursive alternative before a label is chosen -- the match/ematch missing-body fixtures. Every successful parse emits a label instead. Kept in ignored, with type and pattern, so those recovery nodes stay transparent as they always were.
notes.lawDeclaration: Flix v0.75.2 removed law declarations, so Decl.Law left the inventory and the mapping became unreachable -- validateProjectionMap rejects a mapping onto a kind no tree can contain. The grammar still parses `law`, so the rule is declared transparent on our side rather than deleted.
notes.modifier: The reference groups modifiers in ModifierList and holds each as a token, with no per-modifier node, so ours is transparent rather than mapped.
notes.modifierList: Split out of declPrefix so the tree carries the reference ModifierList. Optional in declPrefix, so an absent list leaves no node, as the contract drops empty ones. Its modifier children are ignored and drop out at arity 0, which matches the reference list holding its tokens directly. dropWhenEmpty cannot do this job here: it counts token children, and this projection emits none, so a list holding only `pub` would read as empty and be dropped.
notes.nameLowercase: The reference has one Ident kind and distinguishes case lexically rather than structurally, so all four name rules map onto it.
notes.primaryExpr: Every alternative is labelled (NamePrimary, LiteralPrimary, StringPrimary, HolePrimary, ...). Leaf labels map onto the kind flix-spec expects; container labels (block, record, collection, constraint set) stay ignored, as primaryExpr always was. Before the labels, a token-only leaf projected as a childless primaryExpr that ignored could only drop, which shifted every later sibling: the single largest divergence class. DebugPrimary and HoleVariablePrimary are ignored because their reference kinds are elided at every occurrence. The bare name stays ignored for recovery contexts.
notes.usesOrImports: The reference emits UsesOrImports.UseOrImportList on every file, empty or not; ANTLR omits an optional rule that matched nothing. Declared transparent on both sides, because handling only one side is worse than handling neither -- the other side's wrapper then faces a real node and reports a modelling difference as a disagreement.
